transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… it’s bridges, mostly. If I know I have to cross one, my heart starts pounding before I’m even on it. My hands get damp on the wheel or the armrest, and I get this rush of fear. It’s gotten hard to manage.
Does this fear happen only when you have to cross a bridge?

Mostly, yes. It’s when I know there’s a bridge coming… especially a high one. I know cars go over them all day, but when I see it ahead or even on the map, it feels like it could just drop out from under us.
Are there other places or situations besides bridges that make you feel this same kind of fear?

Not really the same way, no. It’s mainly those high bridges… even just seeing one marked on the map or coming up through the windshield. I know plenty of cars cross them every day, but it feels like it could just drop away underneath us.
Do you also get this fear in other places where it might be hard to get away or get help, like tunnels or crowded public transportation?
No… I don’t think so. Tunnels and crowds don’t really do it like that. It’s the bridges.
